Character Plots and Mysteries
Mark - Kamitos - the Legion
Castle guard, 27, 
lost everything at age 8 (19 years ago), found terrified in his village in a dense fog, village was totally empty elsewise, he still dreams of it
Miralo - village at the west edge of Altuna’s Cup, now said to have been hit by a crop blight and that’s why it’s abandoned. But in reality it’s cordoned off and under constant guard. 
Was adopted by the captain of the group that found him, Finnegan Tealeaf, and moved to Vitrizan
The ghosts appear at times of stress or tension, always look toward Miralo

Finnegan - his father, delighted Kam became a guardsman, raised Kam as his own when they couldn’t have kids, supportive and understanding father, well known and respected and sometimes consulted even though retired, generally relaxed but gets very serious instantly when needed. Entertaining himself with hobbies and trying not to be tempted out of retirement. 

Pella - mother, passed away when he was 17 (10 years ago), sudden death supposedly from a dock infection which seems unlikely, but Finnegan never says any more about it. 

Liara Longthistle - former bully turned close friend, thought ghosts were cool as fuck. 4th or 5th child of an Ambershade noblehouse, halfling, an enabler for Kam. Apprenticed as a wizard, got bored, joined essentially Peace Corps and goes off on state-sponsored adventures. Writes to him sometimes. Cheeky and snobby, kind of obnoxious but skilled, won’t take shit from anyone but Kam (won’t admit that). 


My ideas: Kam witnessed a neighbor house fire as a tot and was traumatized by the death he witnessed, misunderstood the smoke to be mist and vice versa. His birth parents went through a divorce which caused his older brother to lash out, telling Kam ghost stories about monsters in the mist. Mist was normal in the rainy season especially with the streams and the marshes nearby and it being a valley region. Kam wholeheartedly believed in the monsters and grew afraid, so much so that he warned other children and caused a stir in the town. Brother aggravated this by pulling pranks on the little kids with his friends, pretending to be monsters in the mist, or releasing animals like pigs in the village square on misty mornings. The combination of ‘monster’ sightings and Kam’s impassioned storytelling cemented the notion in the minds of all the children of town, them all fully believing in a boogey man the adults couldn’t convince them was fabricated. 

In the center of town was a fountain dedicated to Altuna, standing outside the temple entrance, carved of god-touched stone. It was blessed by Altuna herself and its waters are nourishing, thus used by the temple for healing rituals and crop blessings, etc. But the water doesn’t always flow, only when the priestesses pray does it answer. This wasn’t a fountain of youth, and wasn’t crazily well known across the area, but priestesses would know. So clergy of Altuna would find it odd that there was a crop blight that wiped out the town, and would wonder why Altuna had forsaken the town. 
Brother started telling Kam the mists came from the fountain, and that it was a sign Altuna was angry. His story morphed to say she would send a mist wraith to snatch away the souls she was displeased with, but anyone who sinned against her would be too tainted to pass on in full. The wraith would rip their souls, taking their bodies to fertilize the crops, while their torn souls split in half, one part mixing with the mists to make the wraith bigger, the other part clinging on to the next sinner, and if he died, the souls he’d collected would all travel to the next sinner, etc.

When confronted for tormenting the kids, Brother tried to argue the point of the story was to scare them into behaving, and lied saying he had no part in sending out animals etc on misty mornings to scare the kids. 

There was a priestess of Altuna in training at the time who witnessed all of this, the story telling and the pranks and bullying, but she also noticed Kam wasn’t the only one growing fearful of the fountain as his story spread to other kids. At first she tried to resolve the issue by inviting Kam to pray with her for water to bless the planting season. But in this conversation she mentioned fertilizing the fields, which scared Kam, and as they both put their hands on the fountain to pray, she felt it hum and buzz in a way it never had before for her. Then, mist began to pour out of the top. This scared her, but she didn’t tell Kam to stop, just watched him, and slowly fear shifted to intrigue. She continued watching him and determined that Kam’s belief in his brother’s stories made them real. (She was missing the element that the other kids’ belief was a factor as well). To try and protect him, she invented a story about a special way to protect yourself from the mist wraith and taught the ritual to Kam.

But now that an actual priestess in training was spreading misinformation, the adults began to take the story seriously as well. The priestess in training was punished for the sacrilege of lying about faith to the people, but the damage was already done, as people demanded to be taught her ritual and no amount of high priestesses telling them it wasn’t real would help. Kam tried to share it with the other kids, but the ritual was too complicated for him to remember quite right. As the fervor rose, the priestess in training was dishonorably discharged from service to the temple and publicly shamed. This frightened Kam and infuriated her, to the point she started feeding Kam lies about how everyone here was sinning by treating her this way, and that the next time the mists rolled in, Altuna would reap them. Kam watched her draw a hex sigil over the fountain, too high for him to reach, and she said it would bind the mist wraith here.

So, the next misty morning, Kam’s terror manifested. The mist rolled in naturally at first, then grew thicker. People gathered in the town square, frightened, and the fountain began pouring out mist. Things moved in the mist, this time not caused by Brother. Then the wraith manifested and attacked. The high priestess who had dismissed the priestess in training was killed first. This incited panic, but it was too late. Kam was left panicking and trying to remember the protection ritual while people were torn down left and right. He managed to get it in the end, but by then he was too late to help anyone. The whole village had been killed, and Kam was left with half their souls bound to him. 


Thus, the reason the ghosts always look to Miralo is the other half of their souls are trapped in that mist. The town is under constant guard because there is something hunting in that mist, and because the priestess in training, who used the same protection ritual to survive the attack, found the right connections to propose research into the belief = creation phenomenon she discovered by watching Kam. Kam was adopted out to the Tealeafs to keep him close, unbeknownst to them, but when research into state orphanages showed it wasn’t a power inherent to Kam, they let him be and let him live his life. 

Originally the goal was to use children’s beliefs for good and to avoid ever having another Kam situation where a child’s fears manifested into a monster. Slowly ‘for good’ shifted as politics shifted, and now children are being used ‘for the greater good’, being lied to and tricked into believing in gods that were invented, so that  Ambershade can have a native pantheon. This project is led by the exiled priestess in training, who now fills the High Priestess card position. 


What happened to Pella?
Update - Mark says Kamitos had a younger brother and older sister and married parents, doesn’t look like the divorce plot works or the bully being an older brother. Still want to use the priestess assistant



Chloe - Ace 
Tiefling with Dwarven ancestry, golden horns (god touched by Holgrena)
Five 1/2 years ago Inadvertently killed the eldest child of the most powerful tiefling family in the Sands, the Godeaths, by selling him a bogus revival potion on his way to adventure near the rift. Was exiled for it and had to run off to a backwater fishing town. 
 
Ended up stuck as a parole officer to Masven Godeath, cousin of the Godeath he inadvertently killed. Masven cares more about history than people though and he was really into the idea of expanding the Godeath’ underdark tunnel trade beyond the Sands. A small amount of success caught higher ups’ attention and led to him overpromising wildly while drunk. They sent him to find a safe route to retrieve something in the southern Dynasty, but he ended up in Ace’s town and got arrested. Originally Masven kinda passively wanted Ace dead, but after living with his bullshit for six months he really wants him dead. Masven desperately wants to escape be he’s under watch and can’t get his hands on tools to safely get away. 

Holgrena communicates with Ace and sought to train him in his dreams. She wanted him to be a super mega powerful warlock to turn battle tides in one spell and cement his family in history. His constant rejection and refusal is infuriating, and she still talks to Ace in his dreams, turning them into bloody battlefields as he makes choice after choice to rebuke her. 



My ideas: 
Ace’s parents craved glory and fame, and they prayed to and struck a deal with Holgrena for their son to be made her champion. Something compelled her to agree and attach to Ace, delivering an herb for his mother to consume while pregnant which then made Ace godtouched. Unfortunately Ace doesn’t cooperate with the plan, but Holgrena being the goddess of honor will not go back on her word to make him her champion, which is why she’s still tied to him and pressuring him constantly. 

Holgrena is the goddess of honor and battle, representing order and war. She would be tormented by his disturbing lack of honor. She might like that he’s hanging out with Kam now lol.

Session Notes
Three days ago, each of you had a dream. You were suspended, isolated, within a thick blue-green liquid that wasn’t quite water, tangled up in a red chord. You remember when you reached for it, the dream shattered into fractal images - a bedroom where two fish swam around in a bowl, a meadow where sheep and goats grazed while a lion lazed in the shade, the grand ballroom of the Ambershade’s castle decked out in full regalia for the coronation, but standing empty, all save for a single pedestal in the center of the room, upon which rest a jester’s cap.

You remember the voice that has whispered pleadingly through your dreams for the past few months, hissing around you in a rush of bubbles.
 
Help me. Help me. Find me. Find me. Find me.

Finally, you remember the scene shifted. The ballroom came alive with dancers in formal dress, music resonating through the air, armored guards lining the walls with crests from an array of different nations, while servants wove between tables edging the floor. The music swelled to a grand crescendo, then crashed, bold and final, and in the calm that followed, an ornate cane tapped thrice against the floor of the raised dias at the end of the hall. 

The queen began her speech about harmony and passing the torch to her freshly of age daughter. The princess stepped forward, one hand twisting in her skirts. But you were distracted, first by the sight of three familiar strangers in the crowd, then by a sudden deafening silence that took your mind, and the faint rattle of a little bell.

Help me.

Most of all, you remember the shatter of glass that followed, a deafening roar, and the screech of a terrified girl, echoed soon after by the panicked crowd.

That was how your dream ended. This is how your story begins.


We open on the evening before the gala. It’s mid-spring, officially the second half of the year here in Sunder. The weather is temperate but humid, though the humidity is finally breaking just as the sun kisses the horizon. All around, Vitrizan is vibrant with the scent and sight of Magnolia trees in full bloom. And you, Tem, have just arrived at the palace gate. 

Tem & Mom arrive first at the palace gate, guards direct them toward the stables then the guest entry on the side facing it. Guards at the side door are alarmed that they intend to bring in the drake however, which starts an argument. Witch pushes to be allowed to bring it in, eventually she and Tem can persuade the guards, who then go through the scripted checks. 

Do you have any other protective personnel you’d like to declare?
Are you currently reliant on any means of magic to maintain your body, mind, soul, or spirituality? 
Do you have any metal allergies or moral, ethical, or creed-based objections to metal jewelry?

(To test them, Witch says she does. She’s served a wooden ring instead boo). 

These are souvenir rings made of fine Sudgardian gold and ruby. Within the castle the ruby rings shall suppress all uses of magic as a security measure, providing our esteemed guests with peace of mind and security, as well as a commemorative gift to remember the event. All attendees are required to wear them in order to enter, with exceptions made for security personnel. For security, we have fine gold rings set with amber mined here in the Ambershade Dynasty. These rings allow for the protective use of magic in the unlikely event of an emergency. 

They hand over the appropriate distribution of rings. The one for the drake shifts to fit like a cuff. The guards explain how the rings work and how they can be taken off after leaving the castle grounds.

Inside, Tem and Witch navigate halls with the guidance of the Benjamin Bunswick who explains the gala will begin the next afternoon, and in the tradition of halflings it’ll be an open buffet served by the vendors so they can explain their wares. Witch snerks at that but tells him no no go on. Grumpy, he explains the night will lead up to Princess Briony’s crowning and transition into queen. Then there will be a final waltz, the first waltz of the new reign, then everyone will retire for the evening. Express it is impolite to pursue social networking beyond that time. Witch rolls her eyes at Tem but agrees. 

They get to their room, Benjamin explains he’ll be back to take their dinner orders and leaves them. Witch laughs about that old fuddyduddy, then offers her hand and tells them to use his claw to scratch the wood, just in case. 

goes over key things she wants Tem to do/watch for/pay attention to/care about during the event. [add more here]


Melisande and dignitary (Mythanaar?) arrive just after sunset and are also asked to declare protections and receive rings. Arguments over Ninli can lead to an excuse being given (perhaps one of these guards can be bribed or persuaded to let her in, or she can be claimed as a medical magical need). They’re let in to be escorted by Benjamin. They are asked what they’d like to eat from a dinner menu - salmon, chicken, or mushroom fillet, and a choice of wines, teas, or purified water. The dining hall is being used by the royal family and cannot accommodate guests at the moment, but the service staff will be delivering fine meals to everyone’s chambers.

Mel’s dignitary gets caught up in a conversation schmoozing with Benjamin about his clothes - is that a silken linen? Commentary on the hall portraits and maybe mention of Princess Bellagrace -  while Ninli scurries off around a corner, leading Mel to a pair of people having a hush-hush conversation. She sees the four horned tiefling (Quinn) in conversation with a red headed dwarf who is facing away from her but dressed in find clothes, a long mane of hair cascading down his shoulders, his hands decorated with fine rings and a necklace of precious gems around his throat to match. She catches enough to hear ‘before the last dance.’

Shortly after whatever action she takes here, dignitary will call out to her, forcing her to come back.


The morning of the event comes. 
Kam dreams about Miralo. You were watching your younger self play in the village square, some sort of ball game you only half remember the rules to. You chased after a few of the other children, trying to kick the ball out of their control before they could make a full loop around the fountain in the center of the square in front of the temple to Altuna. It was a simple dream, just children playing, but you wake up in a cold sweat. 

Then gets ready for the day, gets breakfast, goes to his assigned post and awaits Sergeant Abe Hamlet, his squad leader, and for the court mages to come and give them the usual exemption glyphs. But an hour passes and no one has come. The other guards get antsy and start debating what they should do, should they go to the captain of the guard’s office? Would they get in trouble for leaving their post if they did that? Hamlet has a reputation for being emotionally unpredictable and overdrinking in the pub, but he’s never missed his assignments over it. He also has a reputation for tormenting his subordinates by launching surprise tests and punishing them severely if they fail to keep up their expected guard behavior. Everyone’s too afraid to go but also afraid of staying. 

Pressure is put in Kam’s direction. Out of everyone here, Kam is the newest to this squad and hasn’t yet gotten a demerit. Maybe he should go. 

At the office, Riker sits with two boxes of rings and is concerned to hear Hamlet didn’t appear, says Riker just saw a report that he didn’t show for the leadership meeting this morning either and he was supposed to pick up these rings. Explains how they work and that the guards are to wear the amber ones, while Hamlet was supposed to help pass the ruby ones out to the staff. Based on common high opinions of Kam’s work, Riker offers him the leadership role for the night and tells him to take the rings to the butler who will take on the handing out role. Riker will get men on looking for the missing man and do a patrol himself to make sure nothing fishy’s going on, then get into place for the event. The Queen has been very clear that nothing may interrupt this event.


Ace succeeds in getting into the courtyard with his papers and is directed to the staff entrance, a side lot for unloading supplies and such. He’s thanked for his charitable donation to the nation’s prosperity and told to bring his wares into the kitchens and then follow the head of staff, Matthias Fizziewind’s direction from there to be of service during the event and advertise his wares. The Fizziewind asks if he’s going to change into party appropriate attire and if he doesn’t appear to have a prepared outfit for that Fizziewind gets frustrated and snips at him about not following directions, then gives him the ring he’s to wear and sends him off with a human servant to find a service uniform to at least be passable here. Ace immediately notes the ring gem, a ruby, is very easy to fake with simple glass. On investigation, his ring is real. 

Along the way Ace is shown the servant passageways and passes by both the ball room where the coronation will occur and the archmage area where he can get a glimpse of the two orbs to be in use to power the rings (not explained). They stop at a closet within view of that room. Sister Kalista passes through with a gaggle of children, herding them to the ball room in preparation for the gala. They are dressed in simple clothes, seemingly a uniform, and react with nervousness if Ace tries to talk to them (bc tiefling scary). 


The gala begins. Kam is in position along the left wall while Ace is stationed at the buffet by his drinks, the court musicians are playing fanfare as each important figure is introduced. First the nobles of Vitrizan, including Lord and Lady Longthistle and their eldest son Lionel (he gives a slight nod to Kam - Kam knows him to be a studious and accomplished mage, Liara’s primary sibling rival (one sided), and also the second born of the family). Then the other notable figures of the Ambershade are introduced, representatives of a few major tribes and settlements in Laurel Plains, and Priestess Zinnia of Altuna representing Altuna’s Cup, naturally. She is not the Sister Ace saw the other day, but she is immediately followed by Sister Kalista and the gaggle of children, all who are introduced simply as the children of Ambershade. Something about her strikes Kam as off, though he can’t put his finger on it.

At this point, Mel notices the man stepping up for announcement is a red-headed dwarven man. He is introduced as Vassal Hobren Merrymail of the Vassal State of Sudgard. He’s followed by the Vassal of Pikpinem, and then it is Mel’s turn. Her dignitary escorts her to the side, more faces and names are announced - the Nordforg Margrave Donnegral Snowhorn - who is also a red-headed dwarf, the Godeath house head and her husband (uh oh for Ace), the Chamberlain of Calith’Scyne (grumpy), then Tem’s turn as the witch is announced. Kam immediately notes the drake. 

The procession continues, name after name. Tem takes note of a Tabaxi from the Misty Valley. The last people introduced are two members of the Aramyll council of elders, an older wood elf (Imcard) and a middle-aged summer Eladrin (Veladiel). 

The queen gives a speech about this being the last festival celebrating her final hours of reign, talks about how much of joy it’s been to serve her nation and foster the bonds and friendships in this room that shall carry Sunder into a prosperous future. Now drink and be merry. 

The bards take up a jaunty tune, some take to the dance floor while others move to the food table, and the jester Quinn slips into the room. Party has the opportunity to mingle within this space how they’d like. 
Some gossip about Queen Maeleigh being in her 50s and stepping down now - the death of Bellagrace aging her drastically.
Gossip about Briony obviously not being ready for this, rumors of wondering if she’s being pressured into it. Conversations wondering if she’ll be announcing an arranged marriage soon or something.
Rumors about Riker being too close to the royal family. 

Aramyll is receptive and welcoming to the Glade but cautious about Mel and curious as to how she came to the change. 
Emberbloom’s representatives are hitting it up with Glenwood’s, truly embracing the party life and having a grand old time. Icarex Peaks are here too. 
Longthistles are in a polite but judgemental conversation with the governess of Frontier City. 
The Godeath’s are conversing in serious, low tones with the high priestess of the four sisters. 
The Chamberlain of Calith’Scyne is making token interactions with other elves but largely keeping to himself. 
Somewhere in here Ace gets slipped Quinn’s card and instruction to meet him at a dive bar by the docks. 
Sister Kalista is notably avoiding Priestess Zinnia. 

Quinn slips a playing card - the joker - to Ace, inviting him to meet at a dive bar on the docks called the Salty Salmon if he’s looking for work. Show the bartender the card. 

Eventually, the time for coronation comes. The band finishes their song in a swell then the queen taps her cane for silence, the queen and the princess step forward, the jester Quinn tries to exit through Kam’s door while the queen gives a speech. If Kam is still here, Quinn pauses when he seems him squints for a moment, and if asked he’ll say sorry he just had the strangest feeling like I don’t know you from somewhere. Anyway, pardon me. 


The queen gives a speech about passing the torch to a new era of prosperity. Those with good perception notice the rings have loosened on their fingers. The queen steps back, Briony kneels before the throne. The queen takes off her crown. Then crash! The window shatters as a red dragon breaks through. Roll wisdom saves (from fear) and initiative.

(When the coronation speech starts going, the staff in charge of the magic suppressing spell leave the orb in the backroom maintaining it and slip out to help the Players. Shatter is cast to shatter the window, at the same time as illusion spells are cast to make a dragon burst in. — Magician somewhere in the room using the spell Illusory Dragon)

‘dragon’ moves on top of the round (20). Goes to ‘attack’ the princess. Party gets to move while people move to leave and find the doors locked. Riker moves to the princess (nudges her to do her lines) to protect her. Princess drops dramatically to her knees and prays for her nation to be saved.

Illusory magic swirls light and notes of all four seasons around Riker behind her. In seeing this, he rounds on the dragon and raises his sword high just as it draws back and blows ‘fire’ at him. He blocks it all with his sword and one hand. Everyone gets one last round to act, then Riker pushes the flame back at the dragon, which eviscerates it on impact. There’s a beat of silence, then he turns and helps the princess up to her feet. Declares the gods have chosen to serve the Ambershade, and crowns her.

She accepts, then gives a speech about Ambershade being protected but a clear enemy in the midst that poses a threat to their guests, orders the guards to separate the crowd into drawing rooms for questioning - frames it as being for refreshments and just asking if anyone saw anything. Kam’s squad is assigned The Domminae Alliance reps and those of west Ambershade (so not Vitrizan) (this sends Mel and Tem to him) while the staff and vendors are also all directed out the same door so Ace is given an opportunity to cross in with them if he wants. 

The guards are to get a personal statement from anyone who saw anything questionable in the event, and keep everyone put until Captain Riker makes his way in here - after securing the safety of the Royal Family. 

When Riker arrives, he calls Kam over and tells him Abe Hamlet has been found dead in his own home. 


Ace gave up his jester card to the guards.


(Quinn polymorphed into a mouse to slip out of the bathroom and help with thaumaturgy/thunder spell on the window)
